chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from a man, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
The Muḥaddath was mentioned in the presence of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, so he said: “He hears the voice, but does not see the person.”
So I said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, how does he know that it is the speech of the angel?” He said: “He is given tranquility and dignity until he knows that it is the speech of an angel.”

key_terms.السَّكِينَةَ: Divinely granted tranquility and inner reassurance
key_terms.الشَّخْصَ: The visible person or figure, which he does not see
key_terms.الصَّوْتَ: The voice that is heard by the Muḥaddath
key_terms.الْمُحَدَّثُ: One who is spoken to or addressed by the angels without seeing them
key_terms.الْوَقَارَ: Dignity, gravity, and composed assurance bestowed upon him

ai.seo_question: How does a Muḥaddath know that the voice he hears is the speech of an angel?
ai.summary: This hadith explains one aspect of the state of the Muḥaddath: he hears the voice of the angel without seeing the angelic person. It further clarifies that certainty comes through a divinely granted sakīnah and waqār, by which he recognizes that the speech is from an angel.
